narrative.overview:
Sekisho is the checkpoint that inspects every pass. The interface is an After Dark ledger: true-black grounds (or cool white in the light theme), cool white ink with one slight grey for secondary text, ruled with 1px hairlines. One hot red seal ink marks approval acts and nothing else. The operator should always be able to see where they are, what passed and what was stopped; approving something feels like stamping a pass.

It is an operational interface first: dense, legible, built from adapted Shadcn Admin primitives for long sessions in dim rooms beside terminals and editors. The world is carried by material (ink, paper, hairline, seal) rather than decoration. Its finish is native-app calm at the level of macOS and iOS: controls are filled tones rather than outlined boxes, cards are soft 12px sheets, menus grow out of the control that opened them, and the toolbar is translucent. The ledger's data and small labels are set in IBM Plex Mono; its prose stays in Geist. The dark theme is the default (`defaultTheme="dark"`); the light theme is a full cool-white variant with its own tuned values, not an inversion. The implementation lives in `web/src/styles.css` and `web/src/components/`; update the tokens and this document together when an intentional design change is made. There are no marketing illustrations or decorative charts.
keyCharacteristics: Neutral true-black grounds in three steps: darkest sidebar, canvas, raised panels; no warm or tinted cast.
One red seal ink reserved for approval acts; everything else is cool white or near-black ink on its ground, with one slight grey.
Hairlines (border, hairline, input) structure in-flow surfaces; only floating layers cast a shadow.
Filled controls one tone off their surface (`control`), never outlined boxes.
Soft native corners: 8px controls, 12px cards and menus, 16px dialogs; 1.5px seal marks.
Geist for interface and prose; IBM Plex Mono for the ledger voice (figures, IDs, keys, timestamps, chips, column heads, labels); both self-hosted.
One authored motion, the hanko stamp; everything else is short state feedback on native curves.

rules.name: The One Seal Rule
rules.body: Red is the ink of approval: primary actions, the active route, focus, the brand seal, chart ink and activity density. It never decorates, never fills a panel or large field, and never stands in for a status colour; errors are magenta.

rules.name: The Dimmed Seal Rule
rules.body: A disabled primary action keeps its identity but loses its strength: red at 35% with its text at 60%, and no ink-press shadow. Other disabled buttons fade to 50% opacity.

rules.name: The Icon And Word Rule
rules.body: Status colour never travels alone. Every status is a word (Completed, Failed, Verified), never a colour or mark alone; every warning or error paragraph (`p.text-warning`, `p.text-error`) hangs a 16px triangle or circle icon in its inline-start margin through CSS, so wrapped lines keep one clean edge.

rules.name: The Ledger Voice Rule
rules.body: IBM Plex Mono is the voice of the ledger's entries and labels: figures that opt in, IDs, keys, timestamps, status chips, column heads, definition labels, field labels and sidebar group labels. Prose (titles, descriptions, sentences, buttons, menu items) is never mono. Tables, `time`, `output`, `kbd` and `code` set `tabular-nums` globally.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: Every label, including the mono ones, is sentence case. No uppercase labels, and no negative tracking on mono; negative tracking belongs only to Geist titles and the wordmark.

rules.name: The Ruled Page Rule
rules.body: Separate content with a 1px hairline before reaching for a shadow or a nested card. Cards that sit in the page flow carry a border, not a shadow.

rules.name: The Floating Layer Rule
rules.body: Only what floats above the page (menus, dialogs and sheets) casts a shadow, and floating layers use the float shadow's 1px ring instead of a hairline border.

dos: Do reuse the semantic tokens and adapted Shadcn Admin primitives; change `styles.css` and this file together.
Do reserve red for approval acts: primary actions, the active-route seal, focus, the brand seal, chart ink and activity density.
Do dim disabled primaries to red at 35% with 60% text and no shadow.
Do fill controls with the `control` tone; let focus, not a resting outline, draw the seal edge.
Do set figures that opt in, IDs, keys, timestamps, status chips, column heads, field labels and sidebar group labels in IBM Plex Mono, sentence case.
Do name every status in words; colour only flags states that need attention, and no status gets a badge, icon or seal mark.

Do verify the dark default and the light variant, keyboard navigation, narrow layouts, right-to-left Arabic, and the supported languages (English, Japanese, Korean, Spanish, French, German, Portuguese, Russian, Arabic).
Do keep the hanko stamp as the one authored motion and respect `prefers-reduced-motion`.
Do distinguish a planned capability from a working action.
donts: Don't use red as a decorative fill, a panel background, a large field, or a substitute for a status colour; never colour an error red.
Don't add decorative colour gradients, glows, vivid dashboard fills, or arbitrary accent colours; every ground is plain.
Don't load fonts from an external service; Geist and IBM Plex Mono ship with the app.
Don't set prose in mono, uppercase a label, or apply negative tracking to mono text.
Don't draw outlined boxes around buttons or fields, or give in-flow cards a shadow.
Don't alter the seal geometry, recolour it outside the red pair (#D4170F light, #FF3B30 dark), or use the framed seal below 24px.
Don't display fake business records or performance claims.
Don't rely on color, hover, or icons alone for essential information.
Don't expose SDK configuration details in routine team workflows unless users need them to make a decision.
